title: Microbatch choreography: seqlen surgeon for runtime padding reduction
creator: Priya Raman
description: Reduce end-to-end token cost and tail latency by surgically reshaping microbatches based on per-request active token spans and attention phase (prefill vs decode). This ticket scopes a runtime component that (1) derives lightweight 'active-span' fingerprints for incoming requests, (2) groups work into short-lived micro-choreographies optimized for kernel dispatch, and (3) applies minimal trimming/prefix-coalescing only when it yields concrete kernel-level savings without harming cache hit rates.
background: Current batching approach pads to per-batch max sequence length which wastes GPU cycles for workloads with heterogeneous sequences (chat inputs + short triggers + long context). Prior efforts have focused on coarse bucketing or histogram-driven bins, but these either induce scheduler jitter or require heavy bookkeeping. We need a lower-friction mechanism that makes better kernel selection decisions by exposing the request's active token span and attention phase to the scheduler and runtime packer.
design_notes: Introduce a 2-byte ActiveSpan tag that encodes start/end offsets of the request's non-padding token interval relative to the model's input window.
Prefer per-request lightweight annotations over heavy length-bucketing to avoid large blocking queues and to enable more frequent, small micro-choreographies.
Differentiate prefill vs decode kernel targets: prefill benefits from coalescing similar right-aligned spans; decode benefits from eager KV cache reuse and minimal prefix trimming.
Kernel selection policies will consult ActiveSpan histograms per serving shard to choose between fast int8 kernels vs high-throughput cuda kernels depending on effective sequence length distribution.
implementation_plan: 1) Runtime telemetry: emit ActiveSpan histograms and per-shard kernel decision logs (PR: runtime#789).
2) Tagging: add ActiveSpan tagging at request ingress (API layer) and ensure tag propagates to packer/dispatcher.
3) Micro-choreography builder: implement a packer that creates short-lived microbatches by matching compatible ActiveSpan windows and attention phase.
4) Trimming rules: implement conservative prefix trim heuristics that only trim left padding if estimated kernel cycle savings > threshold and KV cache hit degradation < 5%.
5) Kernel policy: add an API for runtime to select kernel implementation based on observed effective sequence length and GPU occupancy.
6) Experiments: run A/B on a subset of traffic to measure token-cost, 95p latency, and cache hit rate.
7) Rollout: gradual traffic ramp, monitor rollback triggers for quality regressions.
acceptance_criteria: End-to-end hourly A/B shows >= 8% token-cycle reduction on mixed-length production workload without increasing mean downstream latency > 2%.
95th percentile latency for decode paths does not regress beyond SLO (compare to baseline) during 1M request sample.
No observable degradation in model output quality from prefix trimming as measured by existing eval set RerankDelta < 0.2%.
Runtime logs expose ActiveSpan histograms and kernel choice events for all serving shards.
Implementation covered by unit tests for packer logic and integration tests for tag propagation.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Overzealous trimming could reduce KV-cache reuse leading to higher token decode cost. Mitigation: conservative threshold + shadow trimming experiment before live trimming.
Risk: Micro-choreography increases scheduling overhead. Mitigation: cap choreography lifetime and batch size; measure scheduler CPU overhead and optimize hot paths.
Risk: Kernel mis-selection on uncommon sequence shapes. Mitigation: fall back to safe kernel and add runtime telemetry to catch frequent fallbacks.
updates: 2026-02-11: Kickoff sync — scoped trimming heuristics to prefill-only for initial iteration. Action: Michael to spike ActiveSpan tag in API proxy (ETA 2d).
2026-02-17: Spike complete — ActiveSpan tag added to request envelope; packer prototype shapes microbatches locally. Observed 6% cycle drop in synthetic mixed-length traffic (shadow run).
2026-02-24: Design review with MLRE — agreed to conservative trim threshold (savings > 12% cycles AND cache hit delta < 3%). Added requirement for RerankDelta guardrails.
2026-03-01: Integration PR for telemetry opened (runtime#789). PM asked to include rollout playbook and rollback SLO metrics.
2026-03-05: Ingress tagging rolled to 10% of traffic behind feature flag. Early telemetry shows microbatch count up 14% and average padded tokens per batch down 11%.
Next steps: complete kernel-selection policy prototype, run 2-week A/B experiment at 20% traffic, validate model quality metrics.
